questions.stem_latex:
A particle moves along a straight line so that its displacement $x$ metres to the right of a fixed point $O$ is given by

$$x=12\ln(t+2)-2t+5$$

where $t$ is measured in seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: What is the inititial position of the particle? Give your answer in exact form.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find an expression for the velocity of the particle at time $t$.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Find when the particle comes to rest.

parts.label: d
parts.latex: What happened to the acceleration eventually?

questions.stem_latex:
Fish are introduced into a small dam. The size of the population, $N$, of fish can be modelled can be modelled by the function

$$N=\dfrac{500}{1+24e^{-0.5t}}$$

where $t$ is the time in months after the fish are introduced into the dam.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Show that the rate of growth of the size of the population is given by

$$\dfrac{dN}{dt}=\dfrac{6000e^{-0.5t}}{(1+24e^{-0.5t})^2}$$

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the range of the function $N$, justifying your answer.

solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{d}{dx}(\operatorname{cosec}x)=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\right)$

$=\dfrac{\sin x\times 0-\cos x}{(\sin x)^2}$

$=-\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin x}$

$=-\cot x\operatorname{cosec}x$

$=\text{RHS}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct quotient rule derivative; 1: simplifies to -cot x cosec x and states = RHS (need both statements)
1: uses log laws to separate; 1: correct derivative

solutions.latex:
$f'(x)=3x^2-6x,\quad f''(x)=6x-6$

Stationary points: let $3x^2-6x=0$, so $3x(x-2)=0$

$\therefore$ stationary points $(0,-1)$, $(2,-5)$

Nature: when $x=0$, $f''(0)<0$, concave down, so $(0,-1)$ is a maximum; when $x=2$, $f''(2)>0$, concave up, so $(2,-5)$ is a minimum.

Inflection: let $f''(x)=0$, so $x=1$. Table: $f''(x)$ is $-$, $0$, $+$ either side of $x=1$.

$\therefore$ point of inflection at $(1,-3)$

\exfigure{1016_q10_s1}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: both stationary points correct; 1: nature of both stationary points correct; 1: point of inflection with test (must have both); 1: correct sketch

solutions.latex:
When $t=0$, $N=\dfrac{500}{1+24}$, so $N=20$

As $t\to\infty$, $N=\dfrac{500}{1+24\times 0}$, so $N=500$

As $\dfrac{dN}{dt}\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$,

$\therefore$ Range $20\le N<500$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: finds limiting value N=500; 1: correct range with justification

solutions.latex:
Let $L=a+b$, where $a=\dfrac{3}{\cos\alpha}$, $b=\dfrac{4}{\sin\alpha}$

$\therefore L=3(\cos\alpha)^{-1}+4(\sin\alpha)^{-1}$

$\dfrac{dL}{d\alpha}=\dfrac{3\sin\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha}-\dfrac{4\cos\alpha}{\sin^2\alpha}=\dfrac{3\sin^3\alpha-4\cos^3\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha\sin^2\alpha}$

Let $\dfrac{dL}{d\alpha}=0$: $3\sin^3\alpha-4\cos^3\alpha=0$, so $\tan^3\alpha=\dfrac{4}{3}$, $\tan\alpha=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{4}{3}}$

Test: $\dfrac{dL}{d\alpha}$ is negative at $47^\circ$, $0$ at $47.7^\circ$, positive at $48^\circ$.

$\therefore L$ is minimised when $\alpha=47.74^\circ$

$\therefore L=\dfrac{3}{\cos 47.74^\circ}+\dfrac{4}{\sin 47.74^\circ}\approx 9.866\text{ m}=9.87\text{ m (2 dp)}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct dL/dα; 1: tan α = cube root of 4/3; 1: test included; 1: L = 9.87 m
